conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I’m feeling a bit off. Just yesterday, I was at the grocery store, and suddenly I felt like something bad was going to happen. My heart raced, and I couldn’t shake the feeling that I was in danger, even though everything seemed normal around me. It’s confusing how quickly that anxiety can hit.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds distressing. In that moment at the grocery store, how did you manage those feelings of anxiety?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I didn't really manage them; I just tried to leave as quickly as I could. I felt a strong urge to get out of there, like I needed to escape. It’s like my mind was screaming that something terrible was lurking, and I couldn't focus on anything else. I just grabbed what I needed and rushed out.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It sounds like the urge to escape was really intense. After you left the store, how did you feel once you got outside?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Once I got outside, it was a little better, but my chest still felt tight, and I kept looking over my shoulder, as if something was chasing me. I thought about how I used to enjoy shopping, but now it feels like a battle every time. I just wanted to get home and lock the door, but a part of me still felt on edge, like the threat was still there.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It's understandable to feel that way. Were there any specific thoughts or images that kept coming to your mind while you were feeling on edge after leaving the store?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Yes, as I was walking to my car, I kept imagining things going wrong, like someone suddenly approaching me or something unexpected happening. It’s like my mind was stuck in this loop, picturing all the worst-case scenarios. I can’t just shake those thoughts off; they cling to me and make everything feel so much scarier.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds really challenging to deal with. In those moments when those worst-case scenarios come to mind, how do you usually respond to them?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: In those moments, I try to distract myself, but it doesn't always work. I sometimes end up replaying the same scenarios over and over, and they just make me feel more trapped. It’s exhausting, and I think I end up avoiding places where I feel like I could get triggered again, like the grocery store. But that just makes everything feel bigger and harder to face.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It sounds like the avoidance is having a significant impact on you. When you think about facing situations like the grocery store again, what feelings come up for you?
